skills.name: Advanced industrial profiles: capabilities and changing employment

note.text: An advanced industrial profile may include specialised suppliers, skilled labour, research, reliable networks and high productivity. These features vary across regions and sectors. Higher output per worker can allow output to grow with fewer workers. A fall in manufacturing’s employment share does not by itself prove that manufacturing output fell. Outsourcing and service growth also affect the shares.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to explain why productivity and employment shares can change differently. Builds on: constraints on industrialisation. Leads to: location models and industrial change.

sections.heading: Explain the geography

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: In an invented comparison, a plant installs efficient equipment and produces more with fewer labour hours. Its productivity rises. A neighbouring research service may support the plant while being counted in services. The sheet’s AIC wording is treated as a school industrial category, not a World Bank income classification or a claim that every region is equally industrialised.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Ask which indicator is changing: total output, output per worker, number of jobs or share of all jobs. Explain a mechanism and acknowledge uneven benefits, retraining needs and environmental costs.

cards.idea: Distinguish the features before applying them.
example: labour productivity: output produced per worker or unit of labour time.
research linkage: connections between investigation, design and production.
employment share: manufacturing jobs as a proportion of all employment.
industrial restructuring: changes in industrial activities, organisation or technology.

cards.idea: Use the evidence in the example, not a place name alone.
example: An invented plant produces more per labour hour.
A laboratory helps a factory improve a process.
Services grow faster while factory job numbers stay unchanged.
A region moves from older heavy plants towards specialised production.

cards.idea: Explain how the process produces the stated effect.
example: Productivity relates output to labour input.
Design support can improve capability without guaranteeing demand.
A share can fall because its denominator grows.
New activities and adjustment costs can be uneven.

pick.r: Total employment grows faster than manufacturing employment

The denominator is total employment.
